title: Frozen boundary rule for the OMO-naming / DSH-only cleanup wave
raw_evidence: raw/04-acceptance-grep-baseline.txt (pre-wave baseline of the acceptance greps: 27 files)
raw/05-consumer-traces-and-floors.txt (writer/reader trace for every kept literal + the hard floors)

method.subject: shipped artifact = a git-tracked path whose first segment is not 'evidence/' (1313 of 4824 tracked files)
method.scan: python/node token-boundary regex identical to BRAND_TOKEN_RE in scripts/build-mcp.mjs:192, applied to every shipped file
method.why_not_substring: a bare `grep -i omo` is unusable: 'autonomous' and 'promote' contain the trigram 'omo'. Every scan in this wave MUST use a token boundary (the guard's own regex), never a substring grep.

R1_boundary_rule.decision_unit: an OCCURRENCE (file:line), never a file: the same file legitimately holds all four classes

classes.definition: a literal whose bytes are read or written by executable code, or are an identifier owned by a third party we do not control, so changing it changes behaviour.
classes.runnable_check: git grep -nF '<literal>' -- <shipped, non-md>; then read the hit: is it an env-key lookup, a socket/JSON key, a session-id parser, a config key, a provider id, an npm scope, or a URL we do not publish?
examples: _omo (writer+reader in one artifact -> RENAME, see allowlist)

classes.definition: a literal that exists so data which ALREADY EXISTS on disk stays readable, or that names a frozen historical record (path, wave id, sha pin).
classes.runnable_check: test -e <path derived from the literal>   OR   a test pins the parser behaviour (e.g. packages/mpd-boulder-plugin/test/boulder.test.ts:22)   OR   the file is under an out-of-scope historical root (R4_out_of_scope)
classes.action: KEEP byte-identical (the user ruling 'history stays byte-identical' outranks tidiness)

classes.definition: a literal that names a THIRD PARTY truthfully: upstream repo slug, commit sha, version tag, package name, licence/copyright text, attribution notice, or a URL that a third party publishes.
classes.runnable_check: git grep -nE 'code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent|8c57e46|5\.0\.0-beta\.20' -- <file>; or the file is LICENSE.md/LICENSE-NOTICES.md/*ATTRIBUTION.md/NOTICE
classes.action: KEEP the FACTS. A provenance sentence may be REPAIRED to be more precise or more truthful, but must never be weakened, and an attribution must never be silently dropped. The informal shorthand (OMO / OmO / omo used as a stand-in for the upstream project in our own prose) is NOT provenance -- it is class 4 and is retired.

classes.definition: everything else: our prose, comments, tool/row descriptions, doc titles, package descriptions, file names, function names, and any code path that exists to integrate with a harness this bundle does not support. Layer D is where BOTH the renames (identity) and the deletions (foreign-harness surface, R3) happen.
classes.runnable_check: it survived classes 1-3 with a citation that can be read at the cited line
classes.action: RENAME to R2 vocabulary, or DELETE when the occurrence names a foreign-harness surface (R3). No third option: 'reword into another foreign name' is forbidden.

R1_boundary_rule.invariant: no occurrence may be classified twice; the allowlist (R3_allowlist) is the exhaustive record of every surviving brand token in a shipped artifact.

R2_vocabulary.zh_note: 专家名录 (used today in packages/mpd-roles-plugin/README.zh-CN.md:4) is NOT the frozen form; use 专家名册 for 'the specialist roster' and 专家阵容 where the ensemble is meant.
R2_vocabulary.upstream_name_rule: the upstream is named by its repository identity (oh-my-openagent, code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent, commit 8c57e46) -- never by the OMO/OmO shorthand, except inside a class 1/2/3 literal.
R2_vocabulary.retired_measured_baseline: 27 shipped files / 38 lines (raw/04-acceptance-grep-baseline.txt); G1 must return 0 after the wave
forbidden_repairs: replacing a foreign harness name with ANOTHER foreign harness name
deleting a provenance fact to make a grep green
leaving a sentence that the rename made false

R3_deletion_rule.definition: A FOREIGN-HARNESS SURFACE is any literal, path, env key, config block, CLI bridge or code path whose only purpose is to interoperate with OpenCode / Codex / Senpi / the OMO CLI. Such a surface is DELETED (not renamed, not documented). A literal is NOT a foreign-harness surface when it merely NAMES a third party truthfully (class 3) or keeps pre-existing on-disk data readable (class 2).
R3_deletion_rule.decisive_test: read the cite: does the code READ/WRITE it in order to talk to a harness this bundle does not ship? -> DELETE. Does it carry a third party's name/URL/licence, or parse a record that already exists? -> KEEP.
R3_deletion_rule.deletion_inventory: raw/03-foreign-surface-inventory.txt (authoritative, file:line per literal); lanes: codegraph=t5, dists/build-mcp=t6, text+skills=t2, doc filenames=t7
R3_deletion_rule.must_not_be_renamed: a foreign-harness surface must not be renamed into an mpd-flavoured spelling: e.g. `.codex/lsp-client.json` must not become `.mpd/lsp-client.json` unless the DSH-native path is independently required (that would be a NEW capability, not a rename).
traps: codegraph reads ITS OWN settings out of the foreign [codex] block (serve.js:9047,9055 harness:"codex") -> a blind deletion silently makes codegraph unconfigurable (always defaults). The retarget MUST be proven behaviourally (sandbox config that disables/configures codegraph, before/after) -- t5 STEP B.

deleting a foreign literal from a REBUILT dist (ast-grep/git-bash/lsp) requires an MPD_SCRUB transform that reproduces the new bytes, because the PRIMARY guard is byte-equality against the committed dist (scripts/build-mcp.mjs:245).

codegraph has NO rebuild script: every edit is surgery and needs `node --check` + a behavioural screen (Note: `node --check` alone does NOT witness a dangling identifier read -- line 8085 EMPTY_OMO_CONFIG parses fine).

R3_allowlist.consumer: reader = that dist (win32 only); writer = the codex installer, OUTSIDE this repo (0 in-repo writers measured)
R3_allowlist.reason: no DSH-side consumer exists, so nothing DSH-side loses a capability; keeping a dead foreign env contract is exactly what the ruling forbids. See R7-C1 -- the t1/t6 acceptance text that says 'stays literal' is the stale side.
R3_allowlist.keep_variant: if the captain/owner overrules C1 and keeps them: the allowlist reason to record is 'external env contract of the upstream omo-codex installer (writer outside this repo); the only reader is packages/mpd-mcp-gitbash/dist/cli.js:320,457-458, win32-only; the DSH-side git-bash MCP row never sets it' -- and t6 must then keep the three BRAND_ALLOWLIST entries as-is.

R3_allowlist.consumer: reader = an editor/JSON-schema resolver fetching the URL; the asset is published by the upstream project
R3_allowlist.reason: renaming a path component of a third party's published asset 404s; it is not our name to change.

R3_allowlist.consumer: HARNESS_KEYS (:7715) -> withoutControlKeys (:7735) strips `[omo]` before MpdConfigSchema (.strict(), :6180-6204) parses it; MpdHarnessIdSchema (:5796-5797) excludes 'omo' as an ACTIVE id, so the entry is inert
R3_allowlist.verdict: CONTESTED -> prefer DELETE via unknown-key stripping
R3_allowlist.reason: the only consumer is acceptance of a legacy `[omo]` section in a pre-existing ~/.mpd/config.jsonc. Deleting the literal is safe IF unknown `[<id>]` sections are stripped before the strict parse; that removes the token AND keeps old configs valid. See R7-C2.
R3_allowlist.keep_variant: if kept: reason to record is 'legacy `[omo]` config-section tolerance: HARNESS_KEYS(:7715) -> withoutControlKeys(:7735) strips it before the .strict() MpdConfigSchema parse (:6180-6204) rejects unknown keys; MpdHarnessIdSchema (:5796-5797) already excludes omo as an ACTIVE id'.

R3_allowlist.consumer: the strict schema accepts them; :9047/:9055 hardcode harness "codex" so OUR OWN settings are read from `[codex]`; :7725 reads OCX_PROFILE/OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR
R3_allowlist.verdict: DELETE the ACTIVE selection (harness:"codex" + the [codex] settings read + OCX_PROFILE/OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR + the [opencode]/[senpi] env paths) and retarget to a project-native block; retain legacy-key tolerance ONLY as strip-before-validate
R3_allowlist.reason: the active path is a foreign-harness surface; the section KEYS survive only as tolerance for configs written by an earlier build of this project. See R7-C2.
R3_allowlist.keep_variant: if kept: reason to record is 'tolerance for ~/.mpd/config.jsonc written by an earlier build of THIS project (our own state path, detectUserMpdJsonPath) -- without the keys the strict parse rejects the user's existing file'. The ACTIVE selection (harness:"codex" at :9047/:9055) is NOT defensible under either ruling and must be retargeted.

R3_allowlist.consumer: normalizeSessionId (shared.ts:13-19) returns an already-prefixed id unchanged; the test pins senpi:x; the file's own :5-8 note calls them data-compatibility values
R3_allowlist.reason: deleting them re-prefixes pre-existing boulder records (senpi:x -> dsh:senpi:x) and breaks resume matching -- a behaviour change, not a rename. The owner's DSH-only bullet was aimed at surfaces, and the write default is already 'dsh'. See R7-C3.
R3_allowlist.keep_variant: already the KEEP verdict; if the owner insists on deletion, the non-regressing form is to keep ACCEPTING the legacy prefixes (the current normalizeSessionId) and change only the comment/test wording -- do not narrow the regex.

R3_allowlist.consumer: the vendored upstream source imports @oh-my-opencode/<core> at build time; the shipped dists are bundled, so it never reaches runtime
R3_allowlist.reason: it is the upstream's own scope; renaming it breaks the offline build's module resolution. Prose around it is class 4 and is rewritten (t6 step 3).

greps.cmd: git ls-files | grep -vE '^evidence/|^(docs/(plan-[a-f]|omo-parity-gap|bline-report|review-p0-p3|track-a-report|ulw-deepseek-optimization)\.md|PLAN\.md|tests/golden/out/)' | xargs grep -nE 'OMO-origin|OMO-derived|OMO specialists|OMO roster|OMO 起源|OMO 名册|OMO 角色|the OMO |upstream omo |\bOmO\b'
greps.allowlist: none -- a hit here is a finding, not a judgement call

greps.cmd: node -e '<BRAND_TOKEN_RE scan over every git-tracked non-evidence file>' and diff the token set against R3_allowlist
greps.expect: every surviving token is an allowlist entry whose `consumer` reads true at the cited line
no pre-existing evidence path is modified (byte-identical history)

greps.note: history keeps the old path by design (R3_allowlist exception + t7 step 4)

greps.expect: declaration and reader agree; `node --check` exits 0 (which alone does NOT prove this -- the ReferenceError is a runtime read)
exit 0, byte-equality guard green, brand guard inspects 4 artifacts (ast-grep, git-bash, lsp, codegraph), negative control fails on an injected token

invariants: re-pin coupling: scripts/verify-vendor.mjs:92-117 fingerprints LOCALLY, so every skills/** edit invalidates assets.skills.fileCount (331) + treeSha and every dist edit invalidates its sha256 -> exactly ONE VENDOR_LOCK re-pin for the wave, in the same commit as the change (AGENTS.md §9/§11), owned by t6
bilingual: every touched human-facing *.md and its *.zh-CN.md sibling change together, each keeping the language switch link directly under the title (G7: python/perl pair check)
dist-vs-src: every plugin whose src changed is rebuilt so dist matches src
mount proof: no --dump-config output may be cited as plugin-load evidence (AGENTS.md §4); the codegraph fix needs a behavioural screen, not `node --check`
no falsified sentence: read each changed sentence; a rename that leaves a false claim (e.g. 'the wire keeps the upstream names ... the `_omo` auth envelope') is a blocker
hash discipline: pin the revision by hash, re-check after a settle window, name the hashes in every verdict (AGENTS.md §7)
